root.name: Rubinstein Opening: Bogoljubow Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Nf3 e6 3. e3 c5 4. Bd3 d5 5. b3 Nc6 6. O-O Bd6 7. Bb2 O-O

overview: White builds the Colle-Zukertort set-up with e3, Bd3, b3, Bb2 and castling while Black replies ...c5, ...d5, ...Nc6 and ...Bd6. The centre stays in tension and White chooses between dxc5, c4 and a Ne5 plan. Neither side commits early, so the game turns on whether White can use e5 and the kingside pieces.

white_ideas.idea: Play c4, Ne5 or dxc5 to challenge the centre
Aim the pieces at the kingside with Ne5 and f4

black_ideas.idea: Break with ...dxc4 and ...e5 for central freedom

typical_structures.structure: Hanging pawns or an isolated queen's pawn after exchanges on c5 and c4

character.notes: A symmetrical-looking set-up where both sides develop and the centre is unsettled.

structure.notes: Pawns on d4 and d5 stay in tension, so the structure is not fixed.

approach.notes: White uses a set-up with Bd3, b3 and Bb2 that works against many defences.

level.notes: The plans matter more than the move order.

character.reason: Neither side has early forcing play, but the pawn tension keeps it from being fully solid.

soundness.reason: Neither side is taking a risk.

structure.reason: The centre is in tension and can resolve either way.

approach.reason: White's set-up with Bd3, b3 and Bb2 is a plan-based system.

level.reason: Plans and pawn-structure choices need understanding, but there is little theory.

plans.reason: The Bb2 sits on the long diagonal and pawn exchanges can leave hanging pawns.
